title: Five notes to explore
summary: Try a smaller set with A at home.

steps.title: Five notes to explore
steps.body:
**pentatonic scale** means a scale with five different notes in each octave. A minor pentatonic uses A, C, D, E and G, then A again. Compared with A natural minor, leave out B and F.

**Why it matters:** Five notes make a manageable set for inventing a short tune.

steps.title: Find the notes
steps.body: Count A, C, D, E, G: five different note names. The last A repeats the home note one octave higher; it is not a sixth different name.

items.prompt: Play A, C, D, E, G, A in that order, one note at a time.

steps.title: Make it familiar
steps.body: Make a tiny tune using A, C and D. Add E and G when those first three feel familiar, and finish on A.

items.prompt: Play A, C, D, E, G, A in that order, one note at a time.
